executiveSummary: Surveillance data from ECDC (Weeks 16-20, April-May 2026) and PAHO (October 2025-May 2026) indicate multiple concurrent biological threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) in the Americas represents the highest-priority BSL-3 select agent concern, with ongoing zoonotic spillover risk flagged in both November 2025 and March 2026 PAHO updates. Additional significant threats include Yellow Fever, Mpox (BSL-3), Dengue, and resurging Measles in the Americas, alongside a Southern Hemisphere respiratory virus season onset. No descriptions were provided in the reports, so threat assessments are based on pathogen identity, alert classification, and known epidemiological context.
bottomLine: Avian Influenza A(H5N1) zoonotic spillover and concurrent Mpox transmission in the Americas represent the most critical select-agent-level biological threats requiring immediate coordinated response.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Two separate PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained zoonotic activity
BSL-3 select agent with pandemic potential and documented human spillover events
Animal-to-human transmission risk persists across multiple American countries
threats.action: Activate enhanced zoonotic surveillance at human-animal interfaces; enforce strict biosafety protocols; coordinate with agriculture and wildlife agencies; prepare antiviral stockpiles and H5N1-specific vaccines for at-risk workers

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 2026 indicating ongoing transmission
BSL-3 select agent with person-to-person and zoonotic transmission routes
Americas-wide circulation requiring coordinated multinational response
threats.action: Strengthen contact tracing and ring vaccination programs; ensure laboratory BSL-3 diagnostic capacity; monitor clade II vs clade I variant distribution; coordinate with WHO and PAHO on case reporting

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 2026 indicating active risk
BSL-3 select agent with high case fatality rate in unvaccinated populations
Sylvatic and urban transmission cycles both represent ongoing threat
threats.action: Verify vaccination coverage in endemic zones; enhance entomological surveillance for Aedes and Haemagogus mosquitoes; ensure adequate vaccine supply; issue travel health advisories for affected regions

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued February 2026 indicating high case burden
Historically record-level dengue activity in the Americas in preceding years with continued elevated baseline
Co-circulation of multiple serotypes increases severe dengue risk
threats.action: Intensify vector control and community engagement; ensure clinical capacity for severe dengue management; monitor serotype shifts; support integrated Aedes aegypti control programs

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and Respiratory Viruses
signals: PAHO alert issued April 2026 marking start of Southern Hemisphere respiratory season
Prior alert in January 2026 flagged simultaneous influenza and RSV co-circulation
ECDC weekly threat reports across Weeks 16-20 indicate ongoing Northern Hemisphere surveillance activity
threats.action: Promote seasonal vaccination uptake in Southern Hemisphere; strengthen ICU surge capacity; monitor for novel influenza reassortants; ensure antiviral availability for high-risk groups

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating active transmission risk
Resurgence linked to pandemic-era immunization gaps and declining herd immunity
Americas region previously achieved elimination status now at risk
threats.action: Conduct vaccination coverage assessments; launch targeted catch-up immunization campaigns; reinforce routine EPI schedules; investigate outbreak clusters for imported vs endemic chains

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two PAHO epidemiological updates issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained upsurge
Post-pandemic resurgence pattern consistent with global trend of increased pertussis activity
Infants and under-vaccinated populations at highest risk of severe disease
threats.action: Enhance Tdap booster coverage especially in pregnant women and adolescents; improve laboratory confirmation capacity; investigate waning immunity and potential pathogen evolution; coordinate national immunization programs

threats.name: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued December 2025 indicating active transmission risk
High case fatality rate (30-40%) with no approved specific treatment
Rodent reservoir activity may be amplified by ecological and climate factors
threats.action: Enhance rodent surveillance and environmental control in high-risk areas; educate rural communities on exposure prevention; ensure clinical recognition training for HPS; maintain diagnostic laboratory access

selectAgentSummary: Three BSL-3 select agents have been flagged across the surveillance period: Avian Influenza A(H5N1) with dual PAHO updates (November 2025, March 2026) indicating sustained zoonotic spillover risk in the Americas; Monkeypox virus (Mpox) with an April 2026 PAHO update confirming ongoing transmission across the Americas Region; and Yellow Fever virus with a March 2026 PAHO alert. All three pathogens require BSL-3 laboratory containment for diagnostic work. H5N1 carries the highest pandemic potential and is assessed as Critical. Mpox and Yellow Fever are assessed as Elevated given current epidemiological activity.
amrSignals: Bordetella pertussis strain evolution potentially contributing to vaccine-modified epidemiology warrants genomic surveillance for macrolide resistance and vaccine antigen divergence
No explicit AMR reports identified in available report titles; ECDC weekly threat reports may contain AMR signals not captured in title-only data
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous onset of Southern Hemisphere respiratory season (influenza + RSV) with ongoing ECDC Northern Hemisphere surveillance creates a global year-round respiratory threat corridor
Dual PAHO H5N1 updates within four months suggest sustained or expanding zoonotic spillover activity rather than isolated events
Post-pandemic immunization debt driving concurrent resurgence of multiple vaccine-preventable diseases (measles, pertussis) across the Americas
Arboviral threat convergence with dengue and chikungunya both active in the Americas increases diagnostic confusion risk and healthcare burden
Repeated PAHO alerts across multiple pathogen categories in Q1 2026 suggest a heightened baseline threat environment in the Americas requiring sustained surge surveillance capacity
